idiom_name: JWTKit: JWTKeyCollection actor with sign(payload, kid:) / verify(_:as:)
implementation_notes: JWTKit is the Swift realization: a struct conforming to JWTPayload types its claims with the library's wrappers (IssuerClaim, SubjectClaim, AudienceClaim, ExpirationClaim, IDClaim) and its verify(using:) method is where the payload validates itself, while JWTKeyCollection - an actor, so key handling is serialized rather than shared mutably - stores signers added with add(hmac:digestAlgorithm:kid:) or the RSA/ECDSA equivalents. What replaces the classic structure: the payload struct plus the key collection replace the builder and the key manager, and the crypto comes from SwiftCrypto (CryptoKit on Apple platforms); issuance becomes an async call because the collection is an actor, and the same collection verifies incoming assertions with verify(_:as:).
pitfalls: Keys registered without a kid overwrite each other - the library keeps only the last one - so during rotation always pass a kid or in-flight assertions start failing verification.
Claim wrappers are types, not enforcement: ExpirationClaim only expires when verify(using:) actually calls verifyNotExpired(), and nothing forces your payload to implement that.
JWTKeyCollection is an actor, so signing is async; calling it from synchronous code forces a Task whose ordering is no longer tied to the caller's state - keep issuance on an async path.
